The database schema named 'rschema_0062' contains three tables: Document, Author, and Modification_Record.
The Document table represents the main documents in the system. It has five columns: Creation_Date (which is a datetime type), Document_ID (an integer type, primary key), Title (a variable character type with a maximum length of 255), Version_Number (also a variable character type with a maximum length of 255).
The Author table is used to store information about the authors. It has six columns: Author_ID (an integer type, primary key), Date_of_Birth (a datetime type), Gender (a variable character type with a maximum length of 255), Name (a variable character type with a maximum length of 255), Phone_Number (a variable character type with a maximum length of 255), and Position (a variable character type with a maximum length of 255).
The Modification_Record table is used to track changes made to the documents. It has six columns: Document_ID (an integer type, not null and a foreign key referencing the Document table), Modification_Content (a variable character type with a maximum length of 255), Modification_Date (a datetime type), Modifying_Author_ID (an integer type, not null and a foreign key referencing the Author table), and Version_Number (a variable character type with a maximum length of 255). The primary key of this table is a composite of Document_ID, Modification_Date, and Modifying_Author_ID.
This schema ensures referential integrity by enforcing foreign key constraints, which prevent deletion or update of records in the Document or Author tables that are still referenced by records in the Modification_Record table. It also ensures entity integrity by enforcing primary key constraints on the tables, and ensuring that all columns allow null values.
gold_question: The Technical Document Management Department manages multiple technical documents, and each document is written by multiple authors. A document has a Document ID, Title, Creation Date, and Version Number. An author has an ID, Name, Date of Birth, Gender, Phone Number, and Position. The document version record needs to record the Modification ID, Document ID, Version Number, Modification Date, Modifying Author, and Modification Content.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0062
CREATE TABLE `document` (
  `creation_date` datetime NOT NULL,
  `document_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `version_number` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`document_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `author` (
  `author_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `date_of_birth` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `gender` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `phone_number` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `position` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`author_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `modification_record` (
  `document_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `modification_content` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `modification_date` datetime NOT NULL,
  `modifying_author_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `version_number` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`document_id`, `modification_date`, `modifying_author_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `modification_record_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`document_id`) REFERENCES `document` (`document_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `modification_record_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`modifying_author_id`) REFERENCES `author` (`author_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
